input:
Labeled defect
- root cause: The shape check before Editor.edit_files tests only for os.PathLike and no longer wraps a plain str, so a string filename is passed on as an iterable and consumed character by character when building the editor command.
- failure path: click.edit(filename="notes.txt") launches the editor with the nine single-character files n, o, t, e, s, ., t, x, t instead of notes.txt; saving creates stray files in the working directory and the intended file is never opened.

Reviewer finding
- description: The check was changed from `isinstance(filename, str)` to `isinstance(filename, os.PathLike)`, so a plain `str` is no longer wrapped in a tuple. The check should cover both `str` and `os.PathLike`.
- rationale: Trigger: `click.edit(filename="file.txt")`. A `str` is not an `os.PathLike`, so it is passed directly to `edit_files` as an iterable of characters. The editor is then launched with one argument per character, such as `f i l e . t x t`, instead of one file. This breaks the most common usage of `filename`.
critique: The finding names the same faulty check: it now tests only for os.PathLike, so a plain str is no longer wrapped and gets iterated character by character. It also gives the same failure, where the editor is launched with one argument per character instead of the single file.
